prompt:
TASK:
            How do you use definite and indefinite forms of nouns in Swedish? Give simple examples.

            PREVIOUS BEST DRAFT (score: 4.0/5.0):
            ---
            Definite form: "barnet" (the child)
Indefinite form: "ett barn" (a child)
            ---

            REVISION INSTRUCTIONS:
            Rewrite the draft above to address the following issues.
            Preserve what was already working well. Do not simply patch — rewrite
            sections where issues are deep.


The following issues MUST be fixed in this revision:
  ✗ [FC-001] Factual Correctness: Incomplete picture by omitting examples of common-gender nouns. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [CC-001] Clarity & Communication: Lacks explanation of when to use definite and indefinite forms. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [DC-001] Depth & Completeness: Insufficient examples and context for the use of noun forms. (flagged 2 times)

            Produce the improved version now. Output only the revised text, no preamble.
generated_text:
Definite form: "barnet" (ett barn) används när du menar ett viss barn, till exempel "min barnet" (ett barn).

Indefinite form: "ett barn" används när du menar en barn, till exempel "ett barn går på skolan" (ett barn går på skolan).

Definite form is used when referring to a specific person, place, or thing. Indefinite form is used when referring to a general person, place, or thing.
